newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian court says can't stop treason trial.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian court says can't stop treason trial.

text.p: A Nigerian magistrate said on Tuesday she could neither hear nor strike out the treason trial of 12 dissidents including self-exiled Nobel Prize-winning writer Wole Soyinka.
The 12, who were charged in March over bomb blasts in Nigeria, face the death penalty if convicted. Only eight of them are in detention.

"My court has no power to entertain or strike out the case but can only urge the police to seek advice from government prosecutors on charging the accused persons at the proper court," said magistrate Adebola Fashanu before adjourning the case to May 23.
Lawyers argue a magistrate court is not competent to hear such a serious charge and say it should be taken to a federal high court or struck out.
Nigerian police have blamed the umbrella opposition group NADECO and its foreign affiliates for the bombings. The groups deny any involvement.
Eight of the defendants were arrested in December after a spate of bomb explosions hit army targets, killing three soldiers and wounding several dozens. They were not present in court on Tuesday.
Along with Soyinka, winner of the Nobel Prize for literature in 1986, others charged in absentia are exiled leaders of NADECO.
The dissidents are charged with "conspiracy to levy war against the federal military government of Nigeria" and "causing explosions in various parts of Nigeria".
On Monday, a bomb blasted a bus taking soldiers to work in the southwestern city of Ibadan, 100 kms (60 miles) from Lagos. Police say no one was injured.
